sowhat.text: Financing got more expensive: the 10-year is back near 5% (4.98%) and a December hike is nearly fully priced, though credit stayed calm (HY 334 bp on Monday). Energy and power asset sales (NRG, CVR) keep coming, and the Anthropic IPO range tests the equity window.

pitch: Stocks slipped on Tuesday. The S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to about 7,520 after October CPI came in hot, 0.4 percent headline against 0.3 expected. The 10-year Treasury jumped 10 basis points to 4.98 percent, and Fed Governor Waller said he leans toward a December hike, which the market now prices at roughly 91 percent for 25 basis points and 9 percent for 50. Oil edged lower, with Brent at about 91.50 dollars and WTI near 86 as Iran tensions eased. On deals, NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion dollars, CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about 4.2 billion, and Marvell is buying Lumentum in a roughly 115 billion dollar stock deal. Anthropic also set an IPO range that could raise up to about 64 billion dollars.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury yield close on Tuesday 10 Nov?
quiz.a: 4.98%, up 10 bp from 4.88% after a hot CPI report.

quiz.q: Why did Treasury yields jump and stocks fall on Tuesday 10 Nov?
quiz.a: October CPI came in hotter than expected (+0.4% headline vs +0.3%, core +0.3% vs +0.2%), and Fed officials including Waller leaned toward a December hike, raising rate-hike expectations.

quiz.q: Who advised CVR Energy on its purchase of two Marathon refineries, and for how much?
quiz.a: Barclays was CVR's exclusive financial adviser; the price is about $4.2B plus working capital.

chat.a: Tuesday's October CPI was hotter than expected, 0.4% headline against 0.3%. The 10-year rose 10 bp to 4.98% and the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,521. A 25 bp December hike is priced at about 91%, with about 9% for 50 bp.
chat.tip: Lead with CPI, then yields, then the Fed.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $91.49 and WTI at $86.04, small declines after Monday's big drop on hopes of easing US-Iran tensions. Brent briefly traded below $90 during the session. That volatility makes it harder for energy buyers and sellers to agree on price.
chat.tip: Name Iran diplomacy as the driver.

chat.a: NRG's $4B sale of six gas plants to LS Power at about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, with Barclays advising NRG. CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about $4.2B, also with Barclays. Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock, with Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman for Marvell and Citi and Evercore for Lumentum.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: PPI comes Friday after a CPI print that put a December hike at about 91% for 25 bp. Treasuries are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day. Next week I'm watching retail sales and Nvidia earnings on 17 Nov, then the FOMC minutes.
chat.tip: Tie PPI to whether CPI was a one-off.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.98% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Companies with most of their value in the terminal value, like growth tech, fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a falling acquirer share price affect a stock deal like Marvell and Lumentum?
chat.a: Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, a premium of about 24%. The ratio is fixed, so a lower Marvell price cuts the dollar value Lumentum holders receive, while the premium was set against earlier prices. Boards may face pressure to revisit terms if the gap widens.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed range is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and a December hike is nearly fully priced. The 10-year is 4.98%, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 334 bp on 9 Nov, so credit is still tight and financing is available at a price.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
